name: meek
why: Hides Tor traffic inside ordinary HTTPS to CDNs, a strange door into censorship-resistant transport design.

brief.what_it_is: Meek is a pluggable transport for Tor, a blocking-resistant way to carry Tor traffic past censors. The Homebrew entry ships two executables, meek-client and meek-server. The scout note says it hides Tor traffic inside ordinary HTTPS to CDNs, but I could not confirm that mechanism from a meek-specific page. The homepage I read is the general Tor Project site and does not describe meek.
brief.why_it_exists: The brew description frames it as a blocking-resistant transport for Tor. I could not reach the meek README or any meek-specific docs, so I have no author framing to quote.
brief.how_it_works: The scout note says meek tunnels Tor traffic inside ordinary HTTPS requests sent to CDNs, so a censor sees ordinary web traffic. I did not verify this against a README, so treat it as unconfirmed.
brief.install_notes: Installed via brew as meek, which provides meek-client and meek-server. I found no README text on setup, configuration, accounts, or first-run steps, so anything beyond brew install is unknown from these sources.
brief.standout: Per the scout note, meek disguises Tor traffic as HTTPS to large CDNs, so blocking it would mean blocking that CDN traffic. It is a different approach from bridges that run on a dedicated address. I could not verify this from the fetched sources.
brief.status: unknown. I found no release date, last commit, or maintenance note. The GitLab repository returned HTTP 403 and the README blob returned a sign-in page.
brief.caveats: The homepage (torproject.org) is the general Tor Project and Tor Browser marketing page and says nothing specific about meek. The GitLab repository returned 403 and the README link led to a login wall, so no meek README was read. The quotes below come from general Tor Project pages, not meek docs. The circumvention page I read is about Tor Browser and bridges, not meek. All mechanism details come from the scout note only.
quotes: Defend yourself against tracking and surveillance. Circumvent censorship.
With Tor Browser, you are free to access sites your home network may have blocked.
To advance human rights and freedoms by creating and deploying free and open source anonymity and privacy technologies
